set.body:
Scope

Make runwise and separate-run/fixed-effects execution safe when the compiled design contains run-local nuisance columns, empty factor cells, or other columns whose support differs by run. The current source-confirmed implementation requires equal predictor counts and positional covariance across runs; a runwise intercept/drift matrix therefore produces zero columns in other runs and fails rank checks, while retained/omitted cells have no explicit shared-effect projection.

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A compiled design exposes a checked per-run coefficient projection that classifies each structural column as shared estimand, run-local nuisance, omitted for this run, or non-estimable.
- [ ] Runwise fitting operates on the run-local numerical axis rather than fitting zero-support global columns; any expansion back to source identity is explicit and reversible.
- [ ] Runwise result types support ragged local axes while preserving stable ColumnIds, run scope, row provenance, rank diagnostics, and chunk merge compatibility.
- [ ] SeparateRunsThenFixedEffects combines only an explicitly declared shared estimand axis; run-specific intercepts, drifts, spikes, and confounds remain per-run evidence and cannot be averaged accidentally.
- [ ] Fixed-effects sufficient statistics carry the projection/mapping used for each run and reject incompatible mappings, fingerprints, weighting policies, or voxel identities before numerical combination.
- [ ] A declared empty cell has an explicit RetainZero, Omit, or Reject outcome per run; retained zero support yields typed non-estimability rather than an opaque solver failure, and omitted support cannot be aligned by position.
- [ ] Cross-run T/F and response-function hypotheses require all selected structural components to be estimable under the declared available-run policy, with a typed diagnostic naming missing or aliased runs/columns.
- [ ] Mixed-TR acquisition grids, censor gaps, run-local baseline/drift, missing cells, complete fitting, and voxel-chunked fitting are observationally equivalent where the estimand is valid on both JVM and Scala.js.
- [ ] Existing common-axis RunwiseLeastSquares and current fixed-effects scenarios remain behaviorally compatible.
- [ ] A public scenario provides an independent small-matrix oracle for the local-axis projection and a receipt explaining any intentional unsupported policy.
set.title: P2.6 follow-up: separate run-local nuisance axes from shared effects
